definition: Diastolic blood pressure is the blood pressure measured during the diastolic phase and is one of the values the autonomic nervous system helps regulate. In this source, it is examined as how that pressure changes between lying down and standing upright during a head-up tilt test.

reasons: The definition states that diastolic blood pressure is “measured during the diastolic phase.” This explanation of what the diastolic phase is/means is not provided in the supplied packet.

While the packet supports that autonomic nervous system regulates blood pressure and that the study examined diastolic blood pressure changes from supine to upright during a head-up tilt test (HUTT), it does not provide the claimed definition of diastolic blood pressure as being “measured during the diastolic phase.”

The source packet supports diastolic blood pressure as a measure used in a head-up tilt test and mentions autonomic nervous system involvement, but it does not define it as blood pressure measured during the diastolic phase.
